llm.summary: The AI trade's first genuine cash-flow crack is now confirmed rather than suspected: Amazon fell 7% because AWS accelerating to +39% was not enough to offset capex guidance that turned free cash flow negative, Alphabet completed the worst single day in its history (~$500B wiped, and Reuters notes its TPU push 'crimps cash flow'), and Big Tech shed nearly $900bn in the rout. Yesterday's hypothesis that hyperscalers were plateauing capex is refuted — they are spending more, and the market is repricing AI from margin-accretive to cash-consuming. Intel plunged ~24% on a weak Q4 guide while simultaneously saying it is 'not able to meet strong customer demand,' which is a capacity story, not a demand story, and is bullish semicap even as it is bearish INTC. Macro is the amplifier: Q3 GDP +3.4%, September PCE at 3.6%, and December rate-HIKE odds at ~75% drove gold below $4,000 and silver below $51 — real rates, not fear, are setting metal prices right now. Energy is the other side of the barbell: Exxon and Chevron beat on soaring diesel refining margins and warned on distillate supply, oil hit a two-week high after a drone strike on a UAE nuclear plant, and Energy flows sit at 90 versus Comm Services at -82. Crypto absorbed its nightmare scenario — a $6.3bn Binance heist with withdrawals halted, plus stolen Polymarket user funds — which transfers value toward regulated venues and custody while damaging the retail flywheel. Nvidia weighing billions in guarantees for Nscale's $45B Anthropic buildout, landing the same week Anthropic filed an IPO prospectus, is the single most important structural development: the buildout is increasingly vendor-financed and reflexive to rates. Within the book, CRM gapped -4.6% into the second leg of the SaaS/agent de-rating and BAX gapped -7.7% on its print.

market_thesis.short_term: Continued compression of long-duration equity multiples with concentrated damage in Comm Services, SaaS and semis, while Energy, Staples, Health Care and Materials absorb the flow. The mechanism is unchanged and now reinforced: 3.4% growth plus 3.6% PCE means the Fed put is gone and December is a live hike at 75% odds. The new variable is that AI capex is visibly consuming free cash flow at Amazon and Alphabet — so the hyperscaler bid for hardware stays intact (bullish NVDA demand, bearish NVDA's customers' multiples) while the equity market demands a discount for cash burn. Expect sell-the-news behaviour to persist even on beats: Sandisk beat, raised and announced an 8-for-1 split and still fell 9%, dragging WDC, STX and MU with it. Month-end and the ISM/payrolls/Apple sequence next week are the next catalysts. Small caps have no bid and Value leads Growth by 66 points.
market_thesis.medium_term: Stagflation (34.4, +15.0) and Reflation (33.5, +14.1) are rising together while Goldilocks collapses — hot nominal growth, sticky prices, rising discount rate. Into H1 2027 I expect the AI complex to bifurcate on financing structure rather than on technology: anyone funded by operating cash flow (Microsoft, Walmart's $6B Symbotic automation deal, utilities) keeps compounding; anyone funded by vendor guarantees, leases and private credit (Nscale, Nebius -26%, Bloom-type levered buildouts) re-rates violently if the December hike lands. Nvidia backstopping a customer's $45B project is textbook late-cycle vendor financing and will become the bear case consensus adopts within two quarters. The software layer stays under pressure because the agentic narrative that used to be an upsell is now read as a threat to seat-based pricing — Alphabet's miss was framed as AI eating search, and that template transfers to every revenue line defined by a query, a seat or an impression. Diesel tightness plus oil supply risk keeps goods inflation sticky and keeps the Fed boxed in.
market_thesis.long_term: Electrons, capacity and physical assets remain the durable supercycle. Nuclear is being pulled forward by data centres with explicit policy support (US pushing expansion in Central Asia and the Caucasus, Finland licensing the first permanent waste site, Temelín switching to Westinghouse fuel), grid and power demand are structurally underbuilt, and semicap benefits from Intel literally being unable to serve demand. Physical AI — Nvidia with Schneider and HPE in process plants, Foxconn's eight-week AI factory deployments, the DSX POD shipping-container datacentre, Symbotic in Walmart's network — converts AI from a software margin story into an industrial capex story with a decade of runway, and tariff relief on robotics imports lowers the cost curve. Against this, a 7.24% mortgage freezes household formation and permanently reallocates a cohort's spend toward value retail, experiences and health; Gen Z telling pollsters the midterms are about 'affording life' is the political expression of the same bifurcation. Crypto's institutional path survives but the retail-custody model took a structural hit from a $6.3bn single-venue theft.

short_term: Trading down in plain sight: Walmart gained 2% on the exact day Amazon fell 7%, and Costco/Temu/dollar-store search attention keeps rising — households are optimising unit price and convenience separately rather than paying one platform for both.

Investors are pulling money from US equity funds ahead of hyperscaler prints while global equity funds take a sixth straight week of inflows — capital is leaving concentrated US mega-cap AI exposure, not leaving equities.

Crypto holders are re-learning counterparty risk: a $6.3bn Binance heist with halted withdrawals plus stolen Polymarket balances pushes behaviour toward self-custody, regulated exchanges and ETF wrappers.
Energy is being bought for cash returns, not growth — Exxon, Chevron and Cenovus beats are being rewarded while AI beats are being sold, an unusual inversion of the normal attention gradient.

Retirees and savers are rethinking decumulation (the 'why not spend' and dividend-income content clusters) as 7%+ mortgages and 3.6% PCE make the real return on cash and bonds the dominant planning input.
Enterprises are buying automation on hard ROI terms — Walmart committing $6B to Symbotic is labour-cost arbitrage with a payback schedule, not an AI narrative purchase.
long_term: Security becomes a purchased good across every digital surface: after the largest crypto theft ever and North Korea's industrialised hacking, custody, verification and identity get priced into the cost of transacting rather than assumed free.
Convenience is being unbundled from trust — consumers will accept slower, more verifiable rails for value storage while demanding instant delivery for goods.
Electricity moves from a background utility to a household budget line people actively search, shop and manage, which is the demand-side precondition for grid, storage and demand-response businesses.

Housing is being substituted rather than solved: with 30-year rates above 7%, a durable cohort redirects housing-denied income into travel, experiences, health and status goods that don't require a mortgage.

Work shifts from seats to outcomes as agents proliferate — software spend migrates toward consumption pricing and toward whoever owns the data and the workflow, which is why incumbents with per-seat models carry a structural multiple discount.
Health moves from episodic treatment to continuous monitoring and metabolic management, sustaining demand for devices and diagnostics even as discretionary budgets compress.

Valuation below own history is not a floor when the terminal revenue model is in question and Comm Services/software flows are the worst in the book. Cut exposure rather than average down; re-engage only when a consumption-pricing transition shows up in reported RPO.

Filed 8-K results and gapped -7.7% — a severe reaction in a sector receiving the second-strongest flows (+57). That divergence says the problem is company-specific execution or guidance, not sector positioning. The 'valuation below own history and below peers' rationale is now a value-trap candidate. Intel's inability to meet demand adds component supply risk. The 'valuation below sector peers' case is intact but the FCF improvement thesis is the one at risk; stress-test gross margin under a sustained memory upcycle.

Results filed with no adverse pre-market gap, into Health Care flows at +57 and a defensive rotation out of Comm Services and Tech. Continuous metabolic monitoring is a structurally rising need and the name carries no AI capex or rate-duration exposure. This is the portfolio's cleanest position in this regime.

Symbotic's $6B Walmart automation contract validates that warehouse and retail automation capex is being funded on labour-cost payback math out of operating cash flow — the most defensible corner of the AI complex. Trump choosing trade talks over tariffs on robotics and industrial machinery removes a cost-of-goods overhang. Industrials flows at -38 cap near-term multiple expansion, so hold rather than add until the flow reading turns.
